Topic.label: Systems of Linear Equations in Three Variables

Question: Solve the system \(\{x+2y+3z=11,\ 2x+3y+z=11,\ 3x+y+2z=14\}\). (Give the values of \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\), in this order, separated by commas.)
Solution: Adding the three equations gives \(6(x+y+z)=36\), so \(x+y+z=6\). Subtracting this from the second equation gives \(x+2y=5\); subtracting \(2(x+y+z)=12\) from the third equation gives \(x-y=2\). Solving these together gives \(y=1\), \(x=3\), and \(z=6-3-1=2\).
